rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for suddenly fleeing or making off.

example.english: As soon as they see the police, the thieves bolt.
example.traditional: 一見到差人，啲賊就走佬。
example.jyutping: jat1 gin3 dou2 caai1 jan4 di1 caak2 zau6 zau2 lou2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday Hong Kong term for a threaded metal fastener, including one used with a nut.

example.english: This bolt needs a nut to be secure.
example.traditional: 呢粒螺絲要配返粒螺帽先至實。
example.jyutping: ne1 nap1 lo4 si1 jiu3 pui3 faan1 nap1 lo4 mou2 sin1 zi3 sat6

rows.note: Use this for the visible flash or spark produced during a lightning storm.

example.english: That bolt of lightning just now was so bright that it lit up the whole room.
example.traditional: 頭先嗰下閃電好光，成間屋都照晒。
example.jyutping: tau4 sin1 go2 haa5 sim2 din6 hou2 gwong1 seng4 gaan1 uk1 dou1 ziu3 saai3

rows.note: Use this specifically when securing a door or gate with its bolt.

example.english: Remember to bolt the door before you leave.
example.traditional: 你記住出門口要閂好道門呀。
example.jyutping: nei5 gei3 zyu6 ceot1 mun4 hau2 jiu3 saan1 hou2 dou6 mun4 aa1

rows.note: Use this for a sliding lock pin or the bar fitted across a door to keep it closed.

example.english: Remember to bolt the door before you go out, so nobody can push it open.
example.traditional: 出門前記住落閂，唔好畀人推門入嚟。
example.jyutping: ceot1 mun4 cin4 gei3 zyu6 lok6 saan1 m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 teoi1 mun4 jap6 lai4

rows.note: Use this for gulping down an alcoholic or other drink quickly, rather than for fleeing or locking something.

example.english: He likes to bolt down a whole can of beer in one go.
example.traditional: 佢成日一口氣隊晒成罐啤酒。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jat1 hau2 hei3 deoi2 saai3 seng4 gun3 be1 zau2
